name: STERIS plc
moat_justification: Narrow/moderate moat: global contract-sterilization (AST) network scale with validated, regulated capacity and geographic redundancy; installed Healthcare sterilizer/endoscopy base pulling recurring consumables and service revenue with real switching friction; regulatory sterility know-how as an intangible barrier; demonstrated pricing power. Against: EO sterilization faces EPA emissions tightening and litigation risk, Healthcare products face large diversified rivals, capital-equipment revenue is cyclical, tariff/inflation cost pressure, growth partly acquisition-bought, and large customers can insource sterilization at the margin.
fragility_flags: NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2024, 2025, 2026 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
one_liner: Quality narrow-moat sterilization franchise (moat 6/10) growing at a guided 7-8%, but at $224.33 the price embeds far more — weighted IRR 8.0%, IV@15% $94.49; clears 15% only at or below $94.49.
moat_for: Global AST contract-sterilization network scale — validated capacity and redundancy device makers rely on
Installed sterilizer/endoscopy base driving recurring consumables + service revenue with switching friction
Regulatory sterility-validation know-how as an intangible barrier to entry
Demonstrated pricing power — price contributed to FY2026 growth
Defensive, non-discretionary demand — infection prevention is mandatory
moat_against: EO sterilization faces EPA emissions tightening and emissions-litigation risk
Healthcare products compete with large diversified rivals (Stryker, 3M, Getinge) on thinner moat
Capital-equipment revenue is cyclical — AST capital equipment fell sharply in Q4 FY2026
Tariff and inflation cost pressure on margins, flagged in FY2026 results
Growth partly acquisition-bought, with heavy intangible amortization
Large device makers can insource sterilization at the margin
